{{Quote|So, friend, what are you looking for? Wait, don't tell me&mdash;I've already got your next droid right here. Why else do you think I sell Otogas?|[[Honest Blim]]|<ref name="TNEGtD" />}}
The '''Otoga-222 maintenance droid''' was a model of [[Maintenance droid/Legends|maintenance droid]] manufactured by [[Veril Line Systems/Legends|Veril Line Systems]]. It was the most common [[Otoga line|Otoga]] variant, having been produced at the height of the line's popularity.<ref name="TNEGtD" />

==Characteristics==
The droid was bipedal and built to take up little space. They could recharge from almost any power source due to the adaptable socket and an internal current regulator. They had hard-shelled bodies and simple gripper hands at the ends of their arms. The small head held a smart and curious electronic brain, which gave the droid an optimistic personality similar to a small child.<ref name="TNEGtD" />

==History==
The Otoga-222 performed heavy lifting and other jobs in [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceports]] and [[Podracer/Legends|Podracer]] [[Hangar/Legends|hangars]],<ref name="IAaD" /> but was outperformed as a [[DUM-series pit droid|pit droid]] by the faster, more manic [[DUM-series pit droid/Legends|DUM-series]]. However, some [[Podracer (profession)/Legends|Podracer]] [[Pilot/Legends|pilots]] preferred the Otoga's steady hands and clear mind.<ref name="TNEGtD" />

The droid was also marketed to households to serve as a general maintenance droid. An advertising campaign during children's [[Holovid/Legends|holovids]] created a great amount of sales with the droids becoming [[Life Day/Legends|lifeday]] presents.<ref name="TNEGtD" />

{{Droid-stub}}

==Behind the scenes==
The Otoga-222 maintenance droid was originally created for the [[1999]] film [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']].<ref name="TPM">{{Film|I}}</ref> Designed by [[Doug Chiang]], it was originally to stand about six [[Foot/Legends|feet]] in height but was shrunk down at the request of [[George Lucas]], who thought the Otoga-222 would be more appealing if it were more childlike.<ref name="TAOTPM">''[[The Art of Star Wars Episode I: The Phantom Menace]]''</ref> Early concept art developed by [[Jay Shuster]] for the [[2002]] film [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']] depicted an Otoga-222 pulling [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] and [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]] in a [[Rickshaw/Legends|rickshaw]], a role ultimately filled by a [[RIC-920 rickshaw droid]] in the final film.<ref name="RIC-920">{{SWArchive|url=episode-ii/bts/design/f20010816/index.html|text=Designs of Ep II: RIC-920}}</ref>
